questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Latvia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Latvia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Latvia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: Latvia's neighbours to the east are the countries Russia and Belarus.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Latvia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: They speak the Latvian language, which is a little like the Lithuanian language but is not close enough to be understood.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Latvia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: Latvia, officially the Republic of Latvia (Latvijas Republika), is a country in Northern Europe.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is one of the Baltic states, together with _____ in the north and Lithuania in the south.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “together”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: It is one of the Baltic states, together with Estonia in the north and Lithuania in the south.
